body:
### Environment
- OS: Windows 11 (LINWEIHAO-PC)
- Magpie: 0.1.1307 (`C:\Program Files\magpie-windows-amd64.exe`, FileVersion 0.1.1307, latest as of 2026-10-21)
- Codex: 0.163.0-alpha.11 (Desktop, `CODEX_VERSION=0.163.0-alpha.11`)
- Model route: `opencode-go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` via magpie gateway `http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1` (`wire_api=responses`), reasoning effort `xhigh`
- MCP: `exa` (`https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp`) and `firecrawl` (`https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp`) both healthy (`tools/list` returns 200)

### What happens
Every `tool_search` call fails before execution when the model emits `limit` as a whole float:

```json
{"query": "exa web search", "limit": 8.0}
```

Codex logs (`~/.codex/logs_2.sqlite`, `codex_core::tools::router`):

```text
handle_output_item_done:build_tool_call: error=failed to parse tool_search arguments: invalid number
```

Followed by:

```text
Tool search output is missing for call id: call_01a15d74439676c7834ceb8d52e77305
```

Same class for other numeric args:

```text
failed to parse function arguments: invalid type: floating point `25000.0`, expected u64
failed to parse function arguments: invalid type: floating point `73472.0`, expected i32
```

Result in UI: `tool_search` always returns `No tools matched the search`, so `web_search_exa` / `firecrawl_search` are undiscoverable. Omitting `limit` (only `{"query": "..."}`) works immediately and both searches return UE 5.8 docs correctly, proving MCP servers are fine.

### Why this matters
- JSON has a single number type: `8.0` and `8` are the same value, differing only lexically.
- Some non-OpenAI providers/models (here: muse-spark via magpie) emit whole floats for integer-valued fields. OpenAI-hosted models usually emit bare integers, so the mismatch is easy to miss.
- Related upstream reports:
  - `openai/codex#33452` — Codex advertises these fields as `"type": "number"` but deserializes as `i32/u64`, so `96230.0` is valid per schema but rejected by parser. Same root cause.
  - `router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI#6237` — request-side fix: rewrite known integer fields from `"type": "number"` to `"type": "integer"` for Codex User-Agent so the model emits `2500` instead of `2500.0`.
  - `router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI#6255` — response-side fix: canonicalize integral float literals in emitted tool-call args (`2500.0` -> `2500`, leave `1.5` untouched, leave strings untouched), with streaming lookahead handling.

### Expected / proposal for magpie
1. Request-side: for Codex clients, rewrite known integer tool params from `number` to `integer` (at minimum `tool_search.limit`, `exec_command.yield_time_ms/max_output_tokens`, `write_stdin.session_id/yield_time_ms/max_output_tokens`, wait timeouts). This steers the model to emit `8` instead of `8.0`.
2. Response-side: canonicalize integral-valued float literals in emitted tool-call arguments before forwarding to Codex (`8.0` -> `8`), same value-preserving rule as #6255. This covers params outside any fixed table and models that ignore schema hints.
3. Either one would fix it; both together matches the CLIProxyAPI approach and is robust to streaming (`function_call_arguments.delta` fragments need bounded lookahead + flush on `done`).

### Repro
1. Codex Desktop + magpie 0.1.1307 gateway, model `opencode-go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor`.
2. Call `tool_search` with `{"query": "exa web search", "limit": 8.0}` (or let the model emit it naturally).
3. Observe `invalid number` in logs and `No tools matched` in UI.
4. Retry with `{"query": "exa web search"}` only — tools `mcp__exa__web_search_exa`, `mcp__firecrawl__firecrawl_search`, etc. are returned.

Happy to provide raw `logs_2.sqlite` rows or a minimal Responses trace if needed. Thanks!
title: [Bug] Tool calls fail when model emits whole floats (e.g. limit 8.0) - Codex strict int parsing
